items.title: Tracking issue: package without source distribution gets an "incomplete" resolution
items.reason: Canonical tracking issue for universal resolution selecting wheel-only releases that cannot install on some platforms. Maintainers explicitly include PyQt5-Qt5 releases without Windows wheels and direct matching PyQt5 reports here.

items.title: uv add fails to install package while  uv pip install doesn't
items.reason: Same Windows `uv add pyqt5` failure, involving PyQt5-Qt5 5.15.16 instead of 5.15.19. A maintainer recommended required-environments; the reporter confirmed it selected Windows-compatible PyQt5-Qt5 5.15.2 and installed successfully.

items.title: resolver: requiring `PyQt5` produces non-portable locks
items.reason: Same dependency and missing Windows artifacts after `uv add PyQt5`. Maintainers explicitly closed it into astral-sh/uv#9711; it documents why Windows wheels for older releases do not make the selected newer release installable.

items.title: Fork when wheels are missing platform support
items.reason: Proposed general platform-based backtracking explicitly covered the PyQt5 case, but was closed without merging. Its discussion identifies the narrower astral-sh/uv#10046 as the change shipped instead.

items.title: Backtrack to non-local versions when wheels are missing platform support
items.reason: Merged December 20, 2024, but only handles local versions such as 2.5.1+cpu and their corresponding base versions. It does not fix selection among ordinary PyQt5-Qt5 releases, so this report does not establish a regression of that fix.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open/closed issues and open/closed/merged PRs with authenticated gh. Literal searches covered PyQt5, pyqt5-qt5, 5.15.19, cp38-abi3-win_amd64, and the missing-source-distribution-or-wheel error. Conceptual searches covered current-platform version selection, required-environments, incomplete universal resolutions, and missing platform support; fix searches also checked closed 0.13.0 wheel reports. PR keyword searches returned no matches; discussion links led to the directly inspected historical PRs. Read candidate comments and followed astral-sh/uv#7005 and astral-sh/uv#8603 through astral-sh/uv#5182, plus astral-sh/uv#9907 to astral-sh/uv#9711. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#19308 as the canonical match because it alleges ignored explicit Windows pins and required-environments, neither reported here; astral-sh/uv#15421 concerns a source-build failure. Also reviewed astral-sh/uv#11865 and astral-sh/uv#11855, repository documentation, and public PyPI release metadata.

type_reason: The same universal-resolution problem is already tracked in open astral-sh/uv#9711, including explicit maintainer discussion of PyQt5-Qt5 on Windows. PyPI confirms that PyQt5 5.15.11 has a Windows wheel, while its dependency PyQt5-Qt5 5.15.19 has neither Windows wheels nor a source distribution. Earlier matching reports establish the required-environments workaround. No regression is established: the general fix was not merged, and the merged local-version fix does not cover these releases.
summary: Duplicate of astral-sh/uv#9711. astral-sh/uv#13299 confirms the same Windows/PyQt5 failure and required-environments workaround; astral-sh/uv#9907 establishes the canonical discussion. Historical PRs did not ship a general fix for this case.
draft_response:
The Windows wheel you found is for `PyQt5`; the error concerns its dependency `PyQt5-Qt5==5.15.19`. PyPI lists only Linux/macOS wheels and no source distribution for that dependency version.

This is tracked in astral-sh/uv#9711. The same Windows/PyQt5 case in astral-sh/uv#13299 was resolved by declaring Windows as a required environment. Add this to your `pyproject.toml`, merging it into any existing `[tool.uv]` section, then rerun `uv add PyQt5`:

```toml
[tool.uv]
required-environments = ["sys_platform == 'win32' and platform_machine == 'AMD64'"]
```

This tells uv to require Windows-compatible wheels during resolution. Please continue discussion in astral-sh/uv#9711.
